Subject: Anchored salary curves & local-market index – proposal and pilot plan

Hi team,

Sharing a concise proposal for how we move from flat geo multipliers to an anchored salary-curve approach across levels (IC2–IC7) and a lightweight local-market index for EMEA pilot countries. Goal: reduce offer variability, simplify approvals, and bake pay equity into offers while minimizing lift for recruiting ops.

Key ideas (TL;DR):
- Anchor points: define three anchor roles per level (core, senior, lead) with market medians. Use anchors to derive a smooth curve (notched bands) rather than discrete slabs.
- Local-market index: compute an index per metro based on cost-of-labor, local benchmarks, and hiring velocity; apply as a multiplier to the curve rather than ad-hoc manual adjustments.
- Equity buffer: reserve a 3% discretionary buffer at offer time for documented pay-equity exceptions (to be tracked in the spreadsheet).
- Implementation: pilot in DE/IE/FR for 8 weeks, paired with updated offer checklist and a one-click recruiter calc in Lever (mockup attached).

Why different: current geo slabs create cliff effects when someone crosses a threshold. Anchored curves smooth movement, make leveling rationale visible to managers, and produce predictable cost projections.

Attachments: anchored_salary_curves_v1.pptx (proposal slides), pay_equity_model.xlsx (calculator), local_index_calculations.csv (source factors).

Open items where I need quick input:
1) Finance: acceptable annualized budget delta tolerance for pilot? (propose <= 1.5% of hiring budget for Q4)
2) People Ops: ok to surface a 3% documented equity buffer in offer notes?
3) Sales/Customer-facing managers: any objections to standardizing curve anchors for client-facing IC4–IC6 roles?

Next steps I propose: 1) confirm pilot scope and finance threshold by Tue 10/06, 2) finalize local-index methodology with CompBench by Thu 10/08, 3) roll pilot comms the week of 10/12.

Thanks — Naomi
